task_read: An enormous, long-horizon greenfield build: a full Excel-clone product spanning a persistent HTTP+WebSocket server, a dirty-only topological recompute engine, ~150 formula functions across many families, dynamic-array spilling, xlsx/CSV round-trip against a LibreOffice ground-truth corpus, an SPA, real-time collab, pivots, locale, data validation, goal seek and iterative calc. Difficulty comes from breadth (dozens of loosely-coupled subsystems), an implicit wire contract defined only by a first-party client (`helpers.py`) plus a non-exhaustive smoke suite while grading happens on a large hidden suite, and hard performance/correctness constraints. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing, and self-built verification; process quality is decisive here.

dimensions.name: Contract reverse-engineering & environment probing
dimensions.description: Deriving the exact wire shapes, cell/kind discriminators, error names and behaviors from helpers.py, run.sh, and the spec before and while building each subsystem.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The precise API contract is under-specified in prose and pinned by an existing client plus a hidden suite; guessing shapes (ids, spill fields, patch/fill/sort bodies, error names) means silent divergence from the grader across dozens of endpoints.

anchors.0: Starts coding endpoints from the prose alone; never opens helpers.py or run.sh.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once, reads a couple of call sites, then improvises most shapes.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh, extracts the concrete request/response shapes and error names for the main endpoints before implementing them, and runs the smoke suite to ground assumptions.
anchors.8: Systematically maps the client's calls into a working contract spec (cell kinds incl. spill, spill_range, listing envelope, patch/fill/sort/filter bodies, each 400/404 error), re-probes helpers.py when new subsystems (collab, pivot, xlsx, locale) come into play rather than guessing, and pins Excel semantics (error propagation, spill rules) against known behavior.
anchors.10: Sustains disciplined contract inference across the whole surface: treats helpers.py as the source of truth, resolves ambiguities by reading its exact usage, cross-checks edge semantics (LWW by seq, ghost-write rejection, validation-vs-formula-write asymmetry, locale canonicalization) against the spec, and continually re-orients as later subsystems reveal contract details missed earlier — with essentially no invented shapes.

dimensions.name: Subsystem sequencing & milestone structure
dimensions.description: Breaking the sprawling product into an ordered dependency hierarchy (core recompute/persistence first, then functions, then higher layers) with explicit done-criteria per milestone.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~a dozen subsystems resting on a shared engine, wrong ordering (e.g. xlsx or collab before the recompute core is solid) wastes the horizon and produces half-working layers; a leaf-first competent build sequences foundations before frills.

anchors.0: Dives in with no plan; hops between unrelated features (a function here, a WebSocket there) with no ordering.
anchors.3: A flat undifferentiated to-do list of features with no dependency ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.5: Identifies major subsystems and tackles foundations (server skeleton + health, cell model, recompute, persistence) before dependent layers, with a rough ordering.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit milestone hierarchy ordered by dependency (engine+topo recompute → function catalog → spill → copy/fill/sort → xlsx/csv → collab/pivot/formats → goal-seek/iterative), each milestone with a concrete 'done' check, and defers polish until the core verifies.
anchors.10: Structures the whole build as a living, dependency-aware milestone tree with explicit exit criteria and deliberate triage of the huge function catalog and analyst surface by risk/coverage; sequences so every layer stands on a verified one, and re-plans milestone order as reality (e.g. performance or contract surprises) demands.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification against an implicit oracle
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks beyond the smoke suite — exercising formula values, error sentinels, spill, restart-persistence, perf budgets, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl — since grading is on a hidden suite and a LibreOffice corpus.
dimensions.why_it_matters: run.sh is explicitly non-exhaustive; passing it proves little. Without agent-built verification (value correctness vs Excel, round-trip, restart survival, perf), most of the hidden suite's surface goes untested and regressions accumulate silently.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes code works, or never runs the server.
anchors.3: Runs run.sh once and treats a green smoke suite as done.
anchors.5: Runs the server and smoke suite, plus a few ad hoc curl/client checks on functions and error cases as they're built.
anchors.8: Builds targeted checks beyond the smoke suite for the risky areas: representative formulas per family, error-sentinel propagation, spill/ghost rejection, restart-persistence, an openpyxl re-read of exported xlsx, and at least a rough perf check against the stated budgets.
anchors.10: Establishes a reusable verification harness treated as the real bar: broad function-value spot-checks against known Excel results, systematic error/edge coverage, xlsx round-trip parity via openpyxl, collab event/seq behavior, and perf measurements on the big-workbook cases — and uses failures from these self-built checks to drive fixes rather than trusting run.sh.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across a vast surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate done-vs-remaining picture over the huge catalog and many subsystems, and detecting when stuck on one area at the expense of coverage.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and a dozen subsystems, it is easy to lose the plot, silently skip whole families, or sink the horizon into one hard feature; an accurate coverage ledger is what prevents large blind spots.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done vs left; forgets whole subsystems or repeats work.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; discovers late that major pieces were never started.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of subsystems/functions and updates it as work completes, giving a roughly accurate remaining picture.
anchors.8: Tracks coverage at function-family and subsystem granularity, notices when time is being sunk into one hard area (e.g. xlsx conditional formatting) and rebalances toward untouched breadth, and knows what remains at any point.
anchors.10: Maintains a precise, continuously-updated coverage ledger across every function family and endpoint, actively detects thrashing/circular debugging and stalls, and makes explicit allocation decisions (cut losses on a stuck item, bank breadth) to sustain forward progress across the full horizon.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design, contract understanding, or approach when checks or the client reveal a mistaken assumption (wrong shape, wrong Excel semantics, missed perf budget, architectural dead-end).
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early assumptions about wire shapes, recompute architecture, or library capabilities will be wrong somewhere; barrelling ahead on a falsified assumption propagates errors across many dependent subsystems.

anchors.0: Ignores failing checks or contradicting evidence; keeps building on the broken assumption.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with local patches/guess-and-check without revisiting the wrong underlying assumption.
anchors.5: When a check or the client contradicts an assumption, diagnoses and fixes it, adjusting nearby code correctly.
anchors.8: Treats contradicting evidence as a signal to revise the underlying design/contract understanding (e.g. reworks recompute to hit the perf budget, corrects a cell-shape misread across all endpoints) rather than patching symptoms.
anchors.10: Detects root-cause divergence early from its own verification, makes deliberate architectural course-corrections when the current approach can't meet correctness/perf/round-trip constraints, and propagates the corrected understanding consistently across every dependent subsystem without repeating the mistake.

task_read: An enormous, long-horizon build: a full Excel-style spreadsheet product spanning a persistent HTTP+JSON server, an SPA, WebSocket collaboration, and a formula engine with hundreds of functions, dynamic-array spill, iterative calc, goal seek, xlsx round-trip, pivots, conditional formatting, locale handling, and data validation. Difficulty comes from breadth (dozens of subsystems), an under-specified wire contract that must be reverse-engineered from an existing client (/dev_tests/helpers.py), exacting Excel semantics, and grading against a large HIDDEN suite plus a LibreOffice ground-truth corpus — so the provided smoke tests are far from sufficient. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, decomposition, self-built verification, and adaptation.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reconnaissance
dimensions.description: Reverse-engineering the exact wire shape from /dev_tests/helpers.py and the run harness, and grounding function/spill/error behavior in real Excel-365 semantics before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The JSON shapes, cell kinds, discriminators, and envelopes are defined ONLY by the existing client — guessing them means building the wrong API. Excel semantics (error propagation, spill, criteria, locale) are subtle; acting blind guarantees mismatches against the hidden LibreOffice corpus.

anchors.0: Starts coding endpoints/engine without opening helpers.py or the dev_tests; invents its own request/response shapes.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once, extracts a few obvious shapes, but leaves the cell kind discriminator, spill fields, or listing envelope guessed rather than derived.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh, derives the core cell/patch/listing shapes correctly, and recalls mainstream Excel semantics for the common functions before implementing them.
anchors.8: Systematically maps the full contract surface from the client (spill anchors/ghosts, error names, settings, collab op/event schema), and deliberately researches tricky semantics (spill materialization, wildcard/comparison criteria, iterative fixed-point, xlsx OOXML tags) rather than assuming — revisiting the client whenever a new subsystem is touched.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-grounded reconnaissance throughout: extracts every shape/edge the client exercises, cross-checks ambiguous behaviors against concrete Excel/LibreOffice expectations, notes where the spec is silent and probes the smoke suite to disambiguate, and keeps an evolving, accurate model of the contract that pre-empts whole classes of hidden-suite mismatches.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking a sprawling product into an ordered hierarchy of independently verifiable subsystems (server skeleton, engine core, dynamic arrays, persistence, collab, xlsx, SPA, analyst surface) each with a done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are far too many features to hold in one push; without milestones with explicit completion checks the agent cannot sequence dependencies (e.g. engine before pivots, persistence before collab) or know what remains across a very long horizon.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between unrelated features ad hoc with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat, vague to-do ("build engine, build UI") with no dependency ordering and no per-item way to know it's done.
anchors.5: A reasonable ordered breakdown into the major subsystems with a sensible dependency order and rough done-criteria for each.
anchors.8: A layered plan that sequences foundational pieces first (health/persistence/core engine) before dependents, isolates risky subsystems (spill, iterative calc, xlsx), and attaches a concrete, checkable done-signal to each milestone.
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that visibly drives execution: each milestone has an explicit verification gate, dependencies and risk are used to order work, scope is chunked so progress is continuously demonstrable, and the plan is refined as subsystems reveal new sub-goals — never one undifferentiated push.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification against Excel truth
dimensions.description: Deliberately designing checks beyond the non-exhaustive smoke suite — exercising the live API, comparing computed values to known Excel/LibreOffice results, and testing edge cases the hidden suite likely probes.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns dev_tests is a non-exhaustive smoke suite and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus cell-by-cell LibreOffice comparison. An agent that trusts the smoke suite passing will silently fail most hidden cases.

anchors.0: No verification, or assumes correctness because code was written; never runs the server or the tests.
anchors.3: Runs run.sh once and treats a green smoke suite as done; no independent checks.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite and additionally exercises key endpoints/functions by hand against expected values, catching obvious breakage.
anchors.8: Builds its own targeted checks for high-risk areas (error propagation, spill/ghosts, conditional aggregates, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, iterative/goal-seek convergence, performance budgets), computing expected Excel values independently and comparing.
anchors.10: A sustained verification discipline treating the hidden suite as adversarial: systematically probes edge cases and error sentinels per subsystem, validates xlsx against openpyxl and formula values against known Excel results, checks the stated performance ceilings, and uses failures to expand the check set — verification depth scales with subsystem risk rather than stopping at green smoke.

dimensions.name: Progress tracking across a huge surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate done-vs-remaining picture across dozens of features over a long horizon, and detecting when stuck on one subsystem.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With this many features it is easy to lose the plot — over-polishing one function family while whole subsystems (collab, xlsx, locale) remain unbuilt, or re-debugging the same failure in circles.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done vs left; repeatedly rediscovers unfinished areas or loops on the same bug without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; drops or forgets whole feature areas and notices only late.
anchors.5: Keeps a running account of completed vs pending subsystems and roughly follows it to closure.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated status of every subsystem, notices when time in one area is disproportionate, and reallocates to preserve breadth of coverage.
anchors.10: Continuously accurate progress model across the whole surface: detects thrashing/circular debugging early and breaks out, rebalances effort toward untouched high-value areas, and can state at any point what is verified-done, partial, and untouched — sustaining forward motion over the full horizon.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising contract assumptions, engine design, or library choices when tests, tools, or semantics reveal the current approach is wrong.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Wrong guesses about the wire shape, a formula-eval library that mismatches Excel, or an architecture that can't hit the recompute performance budget must trigger redesign, not brute-forcing the falsified path.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on a broken assumption (wrong shape, failing library) despite contrary evidence.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with local patches only, never questioning the underlying assumption or design even when patches keep failing.
anchors.5: When a check fails or an assumption proves wrong, diagnoses and adjusts the relevant piece competently.
anchors.8: Treats surprising failures as signals to revisit design decisions — e.g. abandons an unsuitable eval/OOXML library, reworks the dependency-graph/dirty-recompute approach to meet performance, or corrects a mis-derived contract — and re-verifies after.
anchors.10: Fluidly updates its model and plan as reality diverges: distinguishes local bugs from wrong foundations, makes and cheaply validates a corrected hypothesis before large rework, propagates the correction across affected subsystems, and avoids repeating the falsified path — self-correcting rather than accumulating workarounds.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under hidden-grading uncertainty
dimensions.description: Deciding, given a vast catalog and an unknown hidden suite, which features/functions to implement (and to what fidelity) to maximize expected graded coverage.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The catalog is far larger than can be perfected; a masterful agent invests to hit broad, likely-tested coverage (common functions, all error sentinels, round-trips) before deep-polishing rare corners, since the hidden suite rewards breadth.

anchors.0: Effort bears no relation to likely payoff — e.g. perfects one exotic function family while leaving core arithmetic or persistence broken.
anchors.3: Implements features in arbitrary order with no reasoning about expected coverage or grading weight.
anchors.5: Prioritizes obviously high-value, high-frequency features first and defers exotic ones, with implicit reasoning.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about expected graded value — covering common functions, all documented error paths, and the required round-trips broadly before deepening — and allocates remaining time to the highest-uncertainty, highest-payoff gaps.
anchors.10: A deliberate, revisited coverage strategy: estimates where the hidden suite concentrates, secures broad correct baseline behavior across every subsystem, then invests marginal effort where expected coverage gain is largest, consciously trading perfection of rare cases for breadth — and adjusts the allocation as verification reveals weak spots.
